chunks.arabic_text: وَ رَوَى حَمَّادٌ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ:

translations.en: And Ḥammād narrated from al-Ḥalabī, who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَشْتَرِي طَعَامًا فَيَكُونُ أَحْسَنَ لَهُ وَ أَنْفَقَ أَنْ يَبُلَّهُ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يَلْتَمِسَ زِيَادَةً

translations.en: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who buys food and finds it better for him and more marketable to moisten it, without seeking an increase.

chunks.arabic_text: فَقَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ لَا يُصْلِحُهُ إِلَّا ذَلِكَ وَ لَا يُنْفِقُهُ غَيْرُهُ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يَلْتَمِسَ فِيهِ الزِّيَادَةَ فَلَا بَأْسَ وَ إِنْ كَانَ إِنَّمَا يَغُشُّ بِهِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَلَا يَصْلُحُ».

translations.en: He said: “If it is only improved by that, and it is not marketable otherwise, without seeking increase in it, then there is no harm. But if he is only deceiving the Muslims by it, then it is not permissible.”

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the sale of food that is moistened before being sold. If moistening is done merely to preserve or make the food saleable, without intending fraudulent increase, it is allowed; but if it is done to deceive buyers, it is not permissible.
en.seo_question: Is it permissible to moisten food before selling it if there is no intent to deceive?

key_terms.زِيَادَةً: an added increase, especially in apparent weight or amount
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.فَلَا يَصْلُحُ: it is not proper or permissible
